broad_diagnosis.value: Suspected metastatic malignancy involving the liver, with increased hepatic disease burden on follow-up.
broad_diagnosis.basis: Observed: multiple hypoattenuating hepatic lesions, including an ill-defined right-lobe lesion in baseline.nii.gz at native (i,j,k) approximately (185,315,430), and a much larger right-lobe mass in followup.nii.gz around (155,250,542), with additional lesions across k=526-550. Baseline liver reviewed at k=380-440 and follow-up at k=506-558. Multiplicity and marked interval increase favor malignant hepatic involvement, most likely metastases. This is an imaging inference, not histologic confirmation or a known cancer history.
alternatives: Multifocal primary hepatic malignancy
Less likely nonmalignant multifocal hepatic lesions, including infection; unenhanced CT cannot establish histology

public_messages.text: I’ll inspect both volumes in full, review suspicious findings across adjacent slices, and create lesion masks and correspondence groups. I’ll preserve review images and scripts, and document uncertain findings in native voxel coordinates.

The scans have different coverage and slice spacing, so I’m matching findings by anatomy rather than world-coordinate offsets. The clearest finding so far is a right liver mass, more conspicuous on follow-up. I’m checking its baseline extent and reviewing the remaining organs, lungs, nodes, and soft tissues.

I haven’t found a convincing tumor outside the liver in the review so far. Several small nodes and skin folds appear more likely benign or normal. I’m examining the smaller liver findings next, where distinguishing tumor from vessels or cysts is less certain.

The liver review supports one persistent mass and a separate small focus on follow-up that I judge more likely tumor. I also found a new plaque-like area in the right anterior thigh. I’m assessing that separately because its appearance could reflect either tumor or a benign local tissue change.

I’m outlining the liver lesions and checking the masks against the images. I’m excluding the thigh finding because its flat shape and surrounding stranding favor benign local tissue change; I’ll record it as an uncertain excluded candidate. I’m also excluding the small, similar-appearing anterior liver focus, which looks more like a cyst.

The masks currently contain one baseline lesion and two follow-up lesions, with one persistent and one newly appearing group. I’m finishing the image checks and validating that both masks preserve their input grids and that every lesion ID appears exactly once in `events.json`.

Created all four files in [answer](/app/answer/): both instance masks, `events.json`, and [report.md](/app/answer/report.md).

Identified one baseline and two follow-up lesions: one persistent and one newly appearing. Grid and ID consistency checks passed. Uncertainty, evidence, and exclusions are documented; scripts and views are preserved in `/app/work/`.
